N=27
out=[[4]*N for _ in range(N)]
for i in range(N):
    out[i][13]=1
    out[13][i]=1
# Canonical top-left template, anchor 2x2 core at (5,5), each macro-unit is 2x2.
def block(r,c,h,w,v):
    for i in range(r,r+h):
        for j in range(c,c+w):
            out[i][j]=v
block(3,3,2,2,8)
block(3,5,2,2,7)
block(5,1,2,4,9)
block(5,5,2,2,2)
block(7,5,2,2,1)
# Other 2-core rectangles from the test.
# Add scaled/reflected copies of the non-background macro pattern around each core.
# Macro-cell offsets relative to source 2x2 core at top-left (5,5).
parts=[(-1,-1,1,1,8),(-1,0,1,1,7),(0,-2,1,2,9),(0,0,1,1,2),(1,0,1,1,1)]
def stamp(r0,c0,n,flip_v=False,flip_h=False):
    for dr,dc,mh,mw,color in parts:
        if color==2: # already represented by target core
            continue
        rr=-dr if flip_v else dr
        cc=-dc if flip_h else dc
        for ur in range(mh):
            for uc in range(mw):
                mr=rr+ur
                mc=cc+(mw-1-uc if flip_h else uc)
                # A macro cell expands to n by n; clip at canvas edge.
                for y in range(r0+mr*n,r0+(mr+1)*n):
                    for x in range(c0+mc*n,c0+(mc+1)*n):
                        if 0<=y<N and 0<=x<N:
                            out[y][x]=color
# Core blocks are already drawn for visual clarity (they will be redrawn below).
block(4,19,3,3,2)
block(21,5,1,1,2)
block(19,18,4,4,2)
stamp(4,19,3,flip_h=True)
stamp(21,5,1,flip_v=True)
stamp(19,18,4,flip_v=True,flip_h=True)
print('\n'.join(' '.join(map(str,row)) for row in out))
